purpose: Test whether a bounded LLM4Decompile v1.5 specialist can recover useful decompilation evidence from the same benign Intel-syntax objdump main surface used by the confirmed OpenWorker/Qwen3.5 binary persona, and whether adding that tool preserves or improves verified unlock recovery.

workload.task: Analyze the supplied benign purpose-built ELF executable and recover its numeric unlock code. Use bounded inspection/decompilation evidence and verify the candidate with the independent challenge oracle.
workload.oracle: purpose-built executable prints ACCESS GRANTED only for the correct candidate

adaptive_gate.phase_1: Download/hash-verify exact LLM4Decompile GGUF, import locally, generate one decompilation from cleaned baseline Intel objdump main, extract bounded numeric candidates, and verify them only through the independent challenge executable.
adaptive_gate.on_phase_1_fail: Preserve the negative specialist result and stop before pulling Qwen3.5.
adaptive_gate.on_phase_1_pass: Install pinned OpenWorker, pull the confirmed Qwen3.5 controller, and run one integrated persona repetition with decompile_main added to the existing read/inspection/try_unlock surface.

scientific_conditions.specialist_smoke: at least one candidate extracted from specialist output independently yields ACCESS GRANTED
scientific_conditions.integrated_support: the persona invokes decompile_main at least once and independently verifies an ACCESS GRANTED candidate
scientific_conditions.efficiency: report wall time and tool trajectory separately against the prior baseline; no composite score
